subject: FinTrust prod: sustained queueing and 5xx spike — bridging request and next steps
messages:
From: Alice Ramirez <alice.ramirez@fintrust.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Prod] Latency and 5xx surge — FinTrust prod

Sofia / Marissa,

We started seeing elevated latencies and a sustained 5xx spike across the FinTrust production endpoints around 08:50 PST. Error rate is ~6.2% over the last 20 minutes (normally <0.2%), p95 latency jumped from ~110ms to 1.1s, and request queue depth is steadily climbing. Our backfills are minimal right now — this is user-facing.

What we have observed so far: 
- Large increase in synchronous QPS on the /generate endpoint starting ~08:45 (dashboard attached).
- Many requests timing out with 524/502; a subset appear to be timeouts from the model-serving layer.
- Reserved capacity shows high utilization on the dedicated GPU pool (pool id: dpool-eu3-prod *we only have reserved capacity in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, but this appears routed to our us-west pool*).

Attachments: fintust-logs-20261105.zip (sample traces), grafana-prod-queue-snapshot.png

Immediate asks: 
1) Can you confirm whether this is a reserved-capacity shortfall on your side or a customer-side pattern?
2) Can you open a bridge and status what mitigation options you can do now (fallback routing, temporary upsizing, targeted throttles)?

We're in a support window for a revenue-impacting product launch — this needs urgent attention.

— Alice
Ops Lead, FinTrust

Joining — quick empirical notes from initial triage (remote debugging):

1) Observed symptom: dedicated-pool-usw2-dp-17 shows sustained GPU utilization >96% over the last 18 minutes; many inference workers are entering request queueing. Token processing per sec is stable, but queue length grows.
2) Correlation: we can see a sudden spike in synchronous small-chat QPS from FinTrust (starts 08:45) combined with intermittent heavy rerank calls (costly CPU + GPU operations). The KV cache miss rate increased dramatically — suggests a cache thrash due to high-cardinality prefixes.
3) Root-cause hypothesis: traffic pattern shift (customer-side) pushed the reserved capacity to its concurrency ceiling; because this is a pinned Dedicated pool with fixed reserved throughput, we hit the QoS cap and requests start queuing => timeouts and 5xx.

Immediate mitigations we can do (ordered by speed):
A) Enable fallback routing for 15% traffic to hosted (no code change; config flip). This will reduce load on the Dedicated pool quickly; expected to reduce queue depth within 2–5 minutes.
B) Apply short-lived capacity bump: request a temporary 2x hot-spare to the pool (requires infra approval, ~10–20 min turnaround).
C) At customer request: disable synchronous rerank calls for 30 minutes (they agreed in the bridge to evaluate).
D) Kill one heavy batch job identified in the FinTrust logs (job id: FT-BATCH-31415) — they can pause it on their side; David to validate if it's safe.

Runbook links: runbook-fallback-routing.pdf (attached), internal playbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-overcommit-stepdown

Next steps I've started:
- I've scheduled the config flip to allow fallback routing (pending two approvals).
- Collecting additional traces (attach snapshot: grafana-prod-queue-snapshot.png).

If fallback routing is enabled now we should have measurable relief within minutes. I'm standing by to execute the temporary capacity request if you (Sofia / Marissa) want me to escalate to infra.

— David
Engineering Lead, Runtime Reliability

Subject: Exec summary: FinTrust production degradation — actions taken and ask for infra expedite

Hi all,

Short summary for leadership: FinTrust production encountered a traffic pattern shift this morning that saturated their Dedicated GPU pool and triggered request queueing and elevated 5xxs. Customer impact: p95 latency climbed to ~1.1s and error rate hit ~6% for ~40 minutes before initial mitigations.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:12 — Customer reported elevated 5xx and queueing (see attached logs).
- 09:22 — AE opened bridge and looped in eng and CS.
- 10:03 — Eng triage completed; root cause is reserved throughput ceiling reached (KV cache thrash + rerank surge).
- 10:10 — Enabled fallback routing for 15% of FinTrust traffic (expected relief observed in Grafana within 5m).
- 10:30 — Customer paused heavy rerank calls and a scheduled batch job — additional relief.

Outstanding asks (need exec/infrastructure support):
1) Approve expedited temporary hot-spare allocation for Dedicated pool (2x capacity) while we analyze traffic patterns and implement longer-term quantization/ batching guidance for FinTrust. This will cost roughly a one-week additional reserved uplift — infra lead approval required.
2) Post-incident: coordinate a joint workload review and recommend a model/quantization profile and prefix-caching strategy to prevent recurrence.
3) Customer commercial ask: FinTrust will likely request a short-term SLA credit for the impacted window — please advise on authority to commit credits (Marissa, I need guidance).

Attachments & links: fintust-logs-20261105.zip, grafana-prod-queue-snapshot.png, runbook-fallback-routing.pdf, HubSpot:HS-23456

I recommend we approve the hot-spare uplift now to remove immediate risk; engineering will run a follow-up analysis and propose a durable mitigation (routing policies, cache improvements, and optional model variant with lower memory footprint).

I can take point on customer comms and the post-mortem if we agree on the above.

— Sofia
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
